The Cottages at Bridal Falls / Bridal Falls RV Resort — 53480 Bridal Falls Road

A gated bare-land strata resort community. MLS listing records for lots and cottages at this address state the tenure directly: "Title to Land: Freehold Strata," subdivision name "The Cottages At Bridal Falls," zoning CD1, with serviced lots (gas, hydro, water, sewer), concrete pads, and full-time or lock-and-go use; listing text describes it as an "exclusive, gated, bareland strata community" with clubhouse, outdoor pool, hot tub, fitness centre and tennis courts among the amenities, and cottage units on the lots are recorded as single-family / rancher form on freehold strata lots — land and cottage product, not apartment condos, and not counted above. A 2020 developer-era advertisement described the resort as 100 lots on almost 8 acres — advertising copy, carried as such.

items.t: Bridal Falls is a small unincorporated community in the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area D (Popkum–Bridal Falls), east of the City of Chilliwack, near Rosedale and Popkum, at the Highway 1 / Highway 9 interchange area; the FVRD, not the City of Chilliwack, is its local government for planning, zoning, building inspection and bylaw enforcement. The guide page, citing the FVRD's Electoral Area D Housing Needs Report (March 2021), describes Area D as bounded by the Fraser River to the northwest, Electoral Area B to the north and east, Electoral Area E to the south and the City of Chilliwack to the west, and describes Bridal Falls as a highway-services community with several tourist and recreation attractions. An official boundary for the Bridal Falls community itself: Not verified — the guide page states none was found.

Where the strata stock concentrates: at one address — 53480 Bridal Falls Road, the gated bare-land strata resort community the listings call Bridal Falls RV Resort / The Cottages at Bridal Falls. The rest of the guide page's feed snapshot was detached and rural product: four of the five cards read were at 53480 Bridal Falls Road (a rancher and three bare-land strata lots) and the fifth was a new detached house with a legal 2-bedroom suite per its listing text on Lilac Lane in Rosedale.

Transit: BC Transit route 71 (Agassiz–Harrison) runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Harrison Hot Springs through Rosedale, and its on-request trips can route to Bridal Falls — Trip Note B on BC Transit's own Route 71 route-overview page states: "On-Request trips can route to Bridal Falls and/or the Community and Cultural Recreation Centre in Agassiz" — so Bridal Falls is served on request rather than by a fixed stop on every trip; no other BC Transit route serving it was confirmed. The route 71 timetable document (Rider's Guide PDF) itself was not separately opened: Not verified.

Parks and services: Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park, a day-use park on the south side of the Fraser River, 16 km east of Chilliwack, reached by Exit 135 off Highway 1 — the falls tumble 60 metres over a smooth rock face and BC Parks warns the base is extremely hazardous; these park facts are as stated on the guide page citing BC Parks, and verification directly on bcparks.ca is not verified (the host returned a fetch-service 429 pass). Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (FVRD), 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale, is a 107-hectare park of lake, marsh and forest in Electoral Area D where 184 bird species have been recorded and pets are not permitted under FVRD Bylaw No. 1500, 2018. Health care: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, Chilliwack (Fraser Health).

items.t: FVRD plan and zoning — bylaw numbers not verified, stated as such: Chilliwack's OCP and zoning bylaws do NOT apply in Bridal Falls — do not borrow them across the municipal line.

RURAL property taxes govern here — the staged provincial regime, not a city regime: Bridal Falls is unincorporated, so property taxes are levied under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act: taxes in a notice mailed on or before May 31 are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to taxes unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% to taxes still unpaid on October 31 (s. 11). For contrast only — explicitly NON-governing — the City of Chilliwack's second penalty stage falls after August 4, 2026, and the City of Mission's regime is a flat 10% after July 2; neither applies in Electoral Area D.

ALR frame: on ALR land the principal residence maximum is a total floor area of 500 m²; a secondary suite is permitted only when entirely contained within the principal residence and local bylaws permit it; and one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). Parcel-level ALR status for any specific Bridal Falls property: Not verified — confirm on the ALC's ALR maps.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for the park product nearby: pad-rent increases in a manufactured home park are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027. That regime applies to pad tenancies like Mt Cheam's — it does NOT apply to the freehold strata lots at 53480 Bridal Falls Road, which have strata fees instead of pad rent.

items.t: Most of this guide's feed is one address.

Two opposite tenures sit minutes apart and get conflated constantly. At 53480 Bridal Falls Road you buy freehold strata land (no pad rent, SPA governs); at Mt Cheam Mobile Home Park, 52604 Yale Road, Rosedale, you buy a home and rent the pad (MHPTA governs, increases capped at 2.3% plus proportional for 2026 and 2.2% plus proportional for 2027). Listings for both surface under the same Bridal Falls / East Chilliwack searches, and the financing, resale and document packages are entirely different.
The resort's legal details are thinner than its marketing. The Form B package is where a buyer actually learns this community.

Chilliwack's tax dates are the wrong dates here, twice over. Bridal Falls owners pay under the rural Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime — 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31 — even though the mailing addresses on the feed read "Rosedale" and "Chilliwack." A closing adjustment built on the City of Chilliwack's August 4 second stage (or Mission's flat 10%) misstates this community's penalty calendar.

The falls are the landmark and the hazard note in one. Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park is a day-use park reached by Exit 135, the falls drop 60 metres, and BC Parks warns the base of the falls is extremely hazardous with slippery footing and falling rock and ice, and that the falls are prone to freezing into an unstable wall of ice in colder winters — as stated on the guide page citing BC Parks; direct verification on bcparks.ca is not verified (fetch-service 429 pass).
No hazard map was carried for this area.

items.t: Local government / plan — FVRD: Bridal Falls is in FVRD Electoral Area D (Popkum–Bridal Falls); the FVRD provides planning and development approvals, building inspection and bylaw enforcement for its electoral areas — City of Chilliwack zoning does NOT apply here.

Zoning — FVRD: the FVRD sets zoning for Electoral Area D, but the specific FVRD zoning bylaw and the zone of any Bridal Falls parcel were not confirmed on an FVRD source: Not verified — confirm the parcel's zone with the FVRD.

Subdivision and servicing — FVRD: FVRD servicing/bylaw numbers are not verified per the verified ledger — other regional districts' same-letter bylaws are a name collision, NOT citable, and Chilliwack's bylaws are never borrowed for FVRD ground. The process is documented instead: subdivision and servicing questions go to the FVRD as the electoral-area authority; no bylaw number is asserted.

ALR block (where ALR ground is met — parcel status not verified per parcel): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha), subject to local bylaws.

Strata block (the bare-land strata at 53480 Bridal Falls Road): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page — for a bare-land strata lot the Form B package (fees, amounts owing, special levies, CRF balance, insurance, rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement, depreciation report) is what establishes the fees and registered rules; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (a resort with clubhouse, pool and serviced lots carries exactly the common-property assets a depreciation report prices); minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

Taxes — RURAL regime applies (FVRD electoral area, not a municipality): under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11, a 5% penalty applies after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31. Chilliwack's municipal penalty dates and Mission's flat 10% do NOT apply to this ground.

Hazard: the guide page states the published records it read do not list an FVRD or BC document stating a flood or debris-flow hazard for the Bridal Falls area; parcel-level hazard mapping is not verified — check site-specific mapping with the FVRD before building or buying.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Bridal Falls?

Listing records state Title to Land: Freehold Strata and subdivision name The Cottages At Bridal Falls: you own the strata lot, pay strata fees, and the Strata Property Act governs. A pad rental (own the home, rent the land, MHPTA governs) is the product at parks like Mt Cheam on Yale Road in Rosedale. Establish which tenure a listing is before comparing prices across the two.

faq.a: No. Its own listing text says it is mostly senior-occupied but families are allowed — an all-ages, owner-occupied park with no rentals. "Mostly seniors" in listing copy is not an age restriction.
